Mucocele removal

All treated lesions healed in a small mixed-diagnosis series, with no recurrence over a mean 11-month follow-up. The study does not estimate the added effect of PBM over micro-marsupialization alone.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

All treated lesions healed in a small mixed-diagnosis series, with no recurrence over a mean 11-month follow-up. The study does not estimate the added effect of PBM over micro-marsupialization alone.

Summary of the Evidence

One 2012 human case series (11 participants) evaluated laser after micro-marsupialization for oral ranulas and selected mucoceles; the PBM contribution was not isolated. No controlled human, animal or in-vitro study is listed.

Human and clinical evidence

All treated lesions healed clinically, with no recurrence during mean 11-month follow-up. Because diagnoses were mixed and there was no control group, benefit for mucocele removal specifically remains uncertain (Amaral et al., 2012). The series combines oral ranulas and selected mucoceles rather than giving a separate estimate for mucoceles alone. Micro-marsupialization is itself a treatment, and lesions were treated before adjunct laser, so healing cannot be attributed to PBM alone. The mean 11-month follow-up describes recurrence in a small group but cannot estimate a comparative recurrence rate. No sham, untreated, or procedure-only arm isolates the incremental contribution of light. No comparative estimate against excision or another established procedure is available.

Primary original study: Amaral et al., 2012, Low level laser effect after micro-marsupialization technique in treating ranulas and mucoceles: a case series report.. PubMed

Animal evidence

none identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The report specifies a continuous-wave 660 nm InGaAsP diode laser at 100 mW. The 660 nm wavelength is visible red. Treatment followed micro-marsupialization, so these settings describe an adjunct in that small mixed-lesion series and do not define a protocol for excision or PBM alone. Red and blue visible light differ from near-infrared wavelengths, which are outside the visible band.

Interpretation

A small uncontrolled series can support feasibility but cannot show that PBM caused healing or prevented recurrence. The combined diagnoses and the preceding procedure limit generalization to mucocele removal. The evidence does not establish a comparative benefit, a dose-response relationship, or durable outcomes beyond the reported follow-up.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low. One uncontrolled case series combines ranulas and selected mucoceles.
Publications and records1 unique title.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The only direct human evidence is a small uncontrolled case series after micro-marsupialization, with ranulas and mucoceles analyzed together. Lesions healed and no recurrence was reported during limited follow-up, but there was no comparison group. The contribution of PBM to healing or recurrence cannot be separated from the procedure.
